Exercise 15.7.28 — Sketch the Solid Given by an Iterated Integral

Problem. Sketch the solid whose volume is given by the iterated integral ∫02∫02−y∫04−y2dx dz dy. \int_0^2 \int_0^{2-y} \int_0^{4-y^2} dx\, dz\, dy. ∫02​∫02−y​∫04−y2​dxdzdy.

Notation used in this solution

SymbolMeaning
dx dz dydx\,dz\,dydxdzdy Order of integration: the innermost integral is in xxx, the next in zzz, the outermost in yyy.
DyzD_{yz}Dyz​ The projection of the solid onto the yzyzyz-plane: Dyz={(y,z):0≤y≤2,  0≤z≤2−y}D_{yz} = \{(y,z): 0 \le y \le 2,\; 0 \le z \le 2-y\}Dyz​={(y,z):0≤y≤2,0≤z≤2−y}, a right triangle with vertices (0,0)(0,0)(0,0), (2,0)(2,0)(2,0), (0,2)(0,2)(0,2) (in y,zy,zy,z-coordinates).
EEE The solid: every point of DyzD_{yz}Dyz​ is extruded in the xxx-direction from x=0x = 0x=0 to the parabolic surface x=4−y2x = 4 - y^2x=4−y2, i.e. E={(x,y,z):0≤y≤2,  0≤z≤2−y,  0≤x≤4−y2}E = \{(x,y,z): 0 \le y \le 2,\; 0 \le z \le 2-y,\; 0 \le x \le 4-y^2\}E={(x,y,z):0≤y≤2,0≤z≤2−y,0≤x≤4−y2}.

Part 1 — Sketch the solid and state its volume

Step 1.1: Read the bounds from the integral.

The outermost limits give 0≤y≤20 \le y \le 20≤y≤2, the middle limits give 0≤z≤2−y0 \le z \le 2 - y0≤z≤2−y, and the innermost limits give 0≤x≤4−y20 \le x \le 4 - y^20≤x≤4−y2. Hence E={(x,y,z):0≤y≤2,  0≤z≤2−y,  0≤x≤4−y2}. E = \{(x,y,z): 0 \le y \le 2,\; 0 \le z \le 2-y,\; 0 \le x \le 4-y^2\}. E={(x,y,z):0≤y≤2,0≤z≤2−y,0≤x≤4−y2}. The projection of EEE onto the yzyzyz-plane is the triangle Dyz={y≥0,  z≥0,  y+z≤2}D_{yz} = \{y \ge 0,\; z \ge 0,\; y + z \le 2\}Dyz​={y≥0,z≥0,y+z≤2}. At each point (y0,z0)(y_0, z_0)(y0​,z0​) of this triangle the solid extends in the xxx-direction from the plane x=0x = 0x=0 to the surface x=4−y02x = 4 - y_0^2x=4−y02​. Notice that this upper bound is independent of zzz: the far boundary is the parabolic surface x=4−y2x = 4 - y^2x=4−y2, whose trace in the xyxyxy-plane is the parabola x=4−y2x = 4 - y^2x=4−y2 opening toward −x-x−x.

Step 1.2: Identify the bounding surfaces.

The solid has five faces:

  • the bottom face z=0z = 0z=0 (the region 0≤y≤20 \le y \le 20≤y≤2, 0≤x≤4−y20 \le x \le 4 - y^20≤x≤4−y2 in the xyxyxy-plane);
  • the top plane z=2−yz = 2 - yz=2−y;
  • the parabolic surface x=4−y2x = 4 - y^2x=4−y2;
  • the back plane x=0x = 0x=0 (a triangle in the yzyzyz-plane);
  • the front plane y=0y = 0y=0 (the rectangle 0≤x≤40 \le x \le 40≤x≤4, 0≤z≤20 \le z \le 20≤z≤2).

Its five vertices are (0,0,0)(0,0,0)(0,0,0), (4,0,0)(4,0,0)(4,0,0), (4,0,2)(4,0,2)(4,0,2), (0,0,2)(0,0,2)(0,0,2), and (0,2,0)(0,2,0)(0,2,0). At a fixed y0∈[0,2]y_0 \in [0,2]y0​∈[0,2] the cross section perpendicular to the yyy-axis is the rectangle 0≤x≤4−y020 \le x \le 4-y_0^20≤x≤4−y02​, 0≤z≤2−y00 \le z \le 2-y_00≤z≤2−y0​, of area (4−y02)(2−y0)(4-y_0^2)(2-y_0)(4−y02​)(2−y0​).

Step 1.3: Evaluate the volume.

The inner integral gives the length of the solid in the xxx-direction at a point (y,z)(y,z)(y,z):

∫04−y2dx=4−y2, \int_0^{4-y^2} dx = 4 - y^2, ∫04−y2​dx=4−y2,

and the middle integral becomes

∫02−y(4−y2) dz=(2−y)(4−y2). \int_0^{2-y} (4-y^2)\, dz = (2-y)(4-y^2). ∫02−y​(4−y2)dz=(2−y)(4−y2).

Expanding, (2−y)(4−y2)=8−4y−2y2+y3(2-y)(4-y^2) = 8 - 4y - 2y^2 + y^3(2−y)(4−y2)=8−4y−2y2+y3. Hence

V=∫02(8−4y−2y2+y3)dy=[8y−2y2−2y33+y44]02=16−8−163+4=203. V = \int_0^2 \left( 8 - 4y - 2y^2 + y^3 \right) dy = \left[ 8y - 2y^2 - \frac{2y^3}{3} + \frac{y^4}{4} \right]_0^2 = 16 - 8 - \frac{16}{3} + 4 = \frac{20}{3}. V=∫02​(8−4y−2y2+y3)dy=[8y−2y2−32y3​+4y4​]02​=16−8−316​+4=320​.

Result. The solid is E={(x,y,z):0≤y≤2,  0≤z≤2−y,  0≤x≤4−y2}E = \{(x,y,z): 0 \le y \le 2,\; 0 \le z \le 2-y,\; 0 \le x \le 4-y^2\}E={(x,y,z):0≤y≤2,0≤z≤2−y,0≤x≤4−y2} sketched in Fig. 1, and its volume is V=203≈6.6667. V = \frac{20}{3} \approx 6.6667. V=320​≈6.6667.

Step 1.4: Verification by Python.

The script solution/part1_step1.py evaluates the volume in three orders: the given order dx dz dydx\,dz\,dydxdzdy and the two alternative orders dx dy dzdx\,dy\,dzdxdydz and dz dx dydz\,dx\,dydzdxdy. SymPy returns the exact value 20/320/320/3 in every order, and a Monte Carlo estimate with 4×1064 \times 10^64×106 samples gives 6.66406.66406.6640, in agreement. The figure scripts part1_figure1.py and part1_figure2.py produce the two figures embedded above.
